thread:
Sam: quick question — we have a mismatch in routing precedence when a host wildcard + path prefix vs exact path with a header override both match. what's the intended tie-breaker?
Lee: hmm, I thought we did host specificity first, then path specificity, then header matches count. Is that not what's happening?
Maria: seeing the same. Example: host `*.example.com` + path `/api` routes to svc-a, exact host `api.example.com` + path `/api/v1` -> svc-b, but requests to `api.example.com/api/v1` are still landing on svc-a in prod.
TJ: can you paste the rule definitions? maybe ordering in the config file is overriding the comparator.
Sam: here's simplified matcher YAML we have in prod:
```
- match: host: "*.example.com"
  path: "/api"
  service: svc-a
- match: host: "api.example.com"
  path: "/api/v1"
  service: svc-b
```
(we rely on header override `x-target-svc` too)
Lee: oh, order matters currently — we evaluate matchers in file order if specificity scores tie. That bite us before.
Maria: but why would they tie? `api.example.com` is more specific than `*.example.com`.
TJ: scoring bug: host specificity is scored by token count but we treat `*` as 0 tokens. For `api.example.com` and `*.example.com` both end up with same token count because wildcard consumes a token in our parser. I'll open a quick PR.
Sam: we also have header override behavior: if `x-target-svc` is present and matches a service id, it should take precedence unless overridden by route policy. Currently header override applies after route selection which is backwards for many use-cases.
Lee: agreed. Proposed precedence (from highest to lowest): explicit host exact > host wildcard > exact path > prefix path (longest) > regex > header-based override (if flagged allow_header_override) > fallback. But header override should be able to be forced earlier with a per-route `allow_header_override: true`.
Maria: that sounds reasonable. Suggest we implement a deterministic comparator: (host_specificity_score, path_specificity_score, -wildcard_count, header_match_score, route_priority, created_at).
TJ: for clarity, example comparator evals:
```
host_specificity_score(api.example.com)=300
host_specificity_score(*.example.com)=200
path_specificity_score(/api/v1)=200
path_specificity_score(/api)=100
header_match_score=1 if x-target-svc matches service id
```
Then sort desc.
Sam: ok but two more edgecases: trailing slash vs no slash (`/api` vs `/api/`) and service name collisions where header references an alias.
Lee: trailing slash: normalize on register — strip trailing slash except root. That avoids half the problems. For aliases, we should resolve alias -> canonical service id during header-matching step and only accept if service is active in that workspace.
Maria: +1 on alias resolution and workspace scoping. Also we should log when header override is rejected (reason: alias unknown | service inactive | header not allowed).
TJ: I'll push tests. Plan: fix host scoring, add allow_header_override flag (default false), normalize trailing slash, and add detailed logs. Will open PR and include unit tests for these cases.
Sam: thanks. Can we also add a small example in docs for ops that shows how to opt-in header override? People keep writing `x-target-service` incorrectly.
Maria: yes — docs blurb and one-liner curl example. e.g.:
```bash
curl -H "Host: api.example.com" -H "x-target-svc: svc-b" \
  https://edge.redwood.com/api/v1
```
router-bot: matcher-config-change: PR #462 opened by TJ -> staging. Tests: 8/8 passed. :rocket:
Lee: awesome, thanks TJ. Can we roll to canary with the flag disabled by default?
TJ: will do — canary with `allow_header_override`=false, then enable per-route in a small set of routes for 24h.
Sam: great. I'll update the runbook to mention the logging keys to look for (`matcher.override_attempt` + `matcher.override_reason`).
Maria: leaving a note to ops: watch latency spike during canary. Batching logic might change behavior when header override short-circuits routing.
TJ: noted. I'll instrument a histogram metric `matcher.override_latency_ms`.
Sam: cool, thanks all :thumbsup:
